title: Runtime-quality bridge: per-task micro-metric adapters and differential scoring for quant profile rollouts
creator: Asha Menon
description: Implement a lightweight, pluggable "micro-metric" adapter layer in the evaluation harness and runtime telemetry pipeline that computes task-specific fidelity signals for FP8/INT8 quant profiles. These micro-metrics are small, fast-to-compute proxies (e.g., delta-perplexity-on-prompts, MMLU-topic-group accuracy, Rouge-L quick-scan, token-level LM loss drift) intended for continuous validation, canary gating, and automated rollback decisions during rollouts.
background: Current calibration & validation relies on heavyweight eval suites that run offline (full MMLU, BLEU/Rouge batches, human-in-the-loop checks). For Dedicated and Private customers we need a runtime-friendly signal layer that catches regressions earlier and supports faster rollouts. Existing assets: calibration sets curated in Drive (drive.redwood/company/quant/calibration-sets), the evaluation harness repo (github.com/redwood-inference/eval-harness), and the quant-profile registry (runtime-1.18 catalog).
proposal: Build two components: (1) evaluator adapters: small scoring modules integrated into eval-harness to output micro-metrics alongside standard metrics, and (2) runtime telemetry exporters: compute same micro-metrics on sampled production requests (or simulated calibration requests) and push to Console as time-series. Provide default adapters for: delta-perplexity (short prompt cohort), MMLU-mini (10-question per-subject probe), Rouge-L quick-scan for summarization prompts, BLEU-gram-check for translation, and a contrastive n-gram drift score for token-level fidelity. Expose thresholds in rollout config: soft-alert (auto-notify), hard-fail (canary abort).
acceptance_criteria: Eval-harness runs produce micro-metrics as separate output CSV column and JSON lines with metric_id tag
Telemetry pipeline can accept micro-metric events and surface them in Console per-model/per-profile
Two default adapters implemented and tested: delta-perplexity (short prompts) and MMLU-mini
Canary rollout config supports specifying micro-metric thresholds (relative and absolute) and a hard-fail rule
Documentation (Console + SDK + runbook) describing signal interpretation and recommended thresholds is published
implementation_notes: Adapter interface: accepts input batch, returns list of (metric_id, numeric_value) as flat records. Keep implementation single-file per adapter for easy RBAC review.
Metric taxonomy: metric_id format 'micro.<task>.<variant>' (e.g., micro.perp.short_prompts, micro.mmlu.mini_subjects).
Performance target: adapter runtime < 50ms per sample (median) when run in evaluation container; telemetry computation should add <5% CPU overhead on sampler instances.
Storage: micro-metric events stored in metrics store as time-series with tags (model, profile, region, canary_id).

Threshold defaults (initial): delta-perplexity <= 2% relative, MMLU-mini accuracy drop <= 0.6 percentage points, Rouge-L drop <= 1.2 absolute points, BLEU drop <= 1.0 absolute points. These are starting heuristics and must be adjustable per-customer.
metrics: Observer metrics to emit: micro_metric_rate, micro_metric_latency_ms, micro_metric_value (per metric_id)
Signal evaluation rules: rolling-mean over 1h and 24h windows, stdev-based anomaly detection, and a conservative guardrail comparing micro-metric delta to historical noise band
SLO for false-positive canary aborts: <= 0.5% across internal rollout tests
SLO for detection sensitivity: >= 90% detection of synthetic regressions introduced in test branch (bench dataset).
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (internal): run adapters in eval-harness against calibration sets and generate baseline micro-metrics for current production model and candidate quant profiles (one week).
Phase 2 (staging canary): enable telemetry exporters on staging inference fleet with sampling rate 1% and run 48h canary with hard-fail disabled but alerts active.
Phase 3 (limited production canary): enable canary with soft-alerts and hard-fail enabled for critical customers only (opt-in).
Phase 4 (GA): enable default micro-metric monitoring for all rollouts; provide per-customer tuning controls in Console.
testing_plan: Unit tests for each adapter (deterministic inputs -> known outputs).
Integration test: eval-harness end-to-end with micro-metric CSV/JSON output comparing against gold baselines.
Load test: run telemetry exporter under 1000 qps sampler to validate <5% overhead and storage ingestion stability.
Synthetic regression tests: introduce controlled weight-noise in quantized model and verify micro-metric signals cross thresholds in >=90% trials.
